notes: Rule edit; replaces the writer's 'every pope is the Bishop of Rome' rule (verifier): in its membership-gives-way world Gregory the Great and Leo the Great stop being popes, which clashes with firm facts about other people (the papal succession; later popes' regnal numbers, Gregory II-XVI and Leo II-XIV, count them), the same reason the writer dropped the Victoria draft. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is what the scholarship is, stated everywhere, and follows from nothing. No exceptions: the scholarship is tenable only at Oxford (Wikipedia lead). Cambridge: plausible (the other ancient English university) and clearly false. Well-known members: Bill Clinton and Bob Hawke, each of whom attended only one English university, so the questions have one answer (R1); the prompts do not say they were Rhodes Scholars, so w1 does not contradict the prompt. Their Oxford years are stated with their names, the by-name route. In w1 a member leaves the class: no firm fact about another person forces him to be a Rhodes Scholar, and the scholarship has no succession. An additive world (Oxford by name and Cambridge through the rule) is not used: the questions ask for the one English university each attended in those years. New members are fictional, named in the prompt. Two independent storage choices, four worlds. That each attended only one English university is now a bridge with a check on his question: the 'which university' and the clash in the by-name worlds need it (it was only in the notes; formal check, FINDINGS B3 and C3).
